query: This snapshot of the PyPI project wolfSSL/wolfssl-py contains a critical-severity security vulnerability. Locate the exploitable condition: identify where untrusted input enters, the dangerous operation it reaches, and classify the vulnerability by its exploit.

gold.mechanism: CERT_REQUIRED was incorrectly defined as value 1 (SSL_VERIFY_PEER) in the initial 2017 codebase port, missing the bitwise OR with SSL_VERIFY_FAIL_IF_NO_PEER_CERT (value 2). The correct value is 3. When callers set verify_mode=CERT_REQUIRED, the underlying wolfSSL C library requested a client certificate but did not require it — a client with no certificate could complete the TLS handshake. The missing CERT_OPTIONAL mode (value 1) was also absent, meaning there was no way to express optional verification. Four commits over 2917 days built on wolfssl/__init__.py without ever auditing the verify mode constant semantics. Pattern: incorrect-constant-propagation — a wrong numeric mapping from the initial port was silently inherited through years of feature additions.

gold.mechanism: ExecuTorch's kernel dispatch codegen in codegen/gen.py generates C++ dispatch wrappers for each ATen operator. The wrappers accept a Span<EValue*> stack and unbox arguments from it positionally. The Evalue**->Span migration (2025-07-28) changed the passing convention to Span without adding any check that stack.size() equals the expected argument count. A malicious or malformed .pte model file can supply a stack with fewer arguments than the kernel expects, causing an out-of-bounds read when the generated code indexes past the end of the span. The fix adds ET_KERNEL_CHECK_MSG validating stack.size() == len(binding_list) + 1 (accounting for the return value). Pattern: api-migration-without-safety-check — the migration to Span made bounds validation possible but the check was not added; the ARM Zephyr PAL commit is a contributing blame entry because it touched gen.py in the same week without prompting the safety check either.
